page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v7 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Dasv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external block storage attachment.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64as_v7 demonstrates competitive compute and memory capabilities. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng ranks in the top 10%, while multi-core performance falls within the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show strong throughput, reaching 206.82 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 128.87 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database operations are highly efficient, with PassMark database benchmarks placing in the top 10% and Redis SET operations achieving 94.83 million operations per second. For language model workloads, the instance processes small model prompts at 4242.19 tokens per second and generates text on medium models at 44.43 tokens per second, though performance drops to an average tier of 4.65 tokens per second for large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64as_v7 offers a balanced resource profile, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio that avoids the premium costs associated with memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of bundled local storage represents a tradeoff, requiring users to provision external storage, but this allows for precise scaling of storage costs. Given its strong database, compression, and multi-threaded processing benchmarks, this server is suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving, and moderate-scale CPU-based machine learning inference.
